summary.text: A 32-year-old male from Kathmandu valley presented to the Eye Outpatient Department with blurring of vision in both eyes and shortness of breath for 2 days, with daily local alcohol consumption and consumption 2 days prior. He smoked 10 pack years and had no significant past comorbidity. He was referred to the medical outpatient and Emergency departments.

On arrival at the emergency his airway was clear and circulation stable. His vitals were pulse 94, respiratory rate 24, temperature 97.5°F, SpO2 97% in room air and blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, with Glasgow Coma Scale 15/15. Visual acuity was 6/60 in both eyes, fundus and systemic examinations were normal, and arterial blood gas analysis showed severe metabolic acidosis with an osmolar gap of less than 10.

A provisional diagnosis of methanol poisoning was made without a serum methanol level, which could not be assessed. He received oral ethanol via Nasogastric tube and intravenous sodium bicarbonate, was admitted to the MICU and underwent hemodialysis after 4 hours of admission. The urine drug screen detected none of the tested drugs. MRI brain showed acute lacunar infarcts in bilateral posterior putamen and likely optic neuritis.

On day 1 of admission he had no complaints of blurred vision, and bedside visual acuity was normal. He refused advised intravenous methylprednisolone. In the MICU he received folic acid, thiamine and pantoprazole. He moved to the General medical ward on day 3 and was discharged on request on day 5 with thiamine, advised follow-up in ophthalmology, medicine and psychiatry. He was lost to follow-up, but by phone after a week he reported no complaints.
